text.what: James Zellerbach planted two acres of pinot noir and four of chardonnay above Sonoma in 1953, then built a cellar copying Burgundy's methods — French oak, temperature control, inert gas. California winemaking followed him.

kin.as: Among the earliest serious American plantings after Prohibition.
The barrel question he answered by importing the barrels.
